author: product-requirements-expert
title: Filter the veterinarian directory by specialty on both surfaces
summary: Both vet directory surfaces accept an optional specialty filter supplied only through the request URL: the paged HTML page and the reinstated JSON endpoint each show only veterinarians holding the named specialty. Matching is on the whole name, case-insensitive.
acceptance_criteria: Filtering the paged page by a held specialty lists only those veterinarians, with paging applied to the narrowed list
Requesting the JSON endpoint with a held specialty returns only those veterinarians
A specialty differing from a stored name only by letter case matches on either surface
A value that is only a prefix of a specialty name and not the whole name matches no veterinarian
A specialty matching no veterinarian returns the ordinary page or JSON document with an empty veterinarian list and a success status
A blank or whitespace-only specialty behaves as the same request with no specialty
With no specialty, either surface behaves as it does today
A narrowed result spanning more than one page keeps the specialty when a paging link is followed
The filter is driven only through the request URL; neither surface presents a form, dropdown, or other page control for it
non_goals: A visible filter control (form or dropdown) on either surface
Filtering by more than one specialty at once
notes: Narrows NG-9 (see adr/2026-08-23-non-goal-vet-specialty-filter.md). Reinstates the JSON endpoint as a supported surface; REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused. JSON endpoint returns the filtered list in its prior unpaged shape. Open questions recorded in the PRD: multi-specialty filtering and a future visible control. May be split into an HTML-page slice and a JSON-endpoint slice under this same req_id if design judges it too large; they share the specialty-matching core.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Ships whole (one slice, both surfaces), not split: the two surfaces share one small matching core, so splitting would duplicate the core or create an awkward inter-slice dependency for negligible risk reduction. The filter runs in-code over the cached full vet collection rather than via a repository query — new design ground recorded in ADR 2026-08-23-vet-specialty-filter-in-controller.md and in system-design.md#contracts (Vet Contracts row, new 'Vet specialty filter' note). It reuses the existing @Cacheable('vets') full-list read (VetRepository.findAll()) and the in-force Web-controller and Aggregate patterns from architecture-principles.md; the matching rule lands on the Vet aggregate, keeping it out of the controller. The JSON /vets surface is reinstated as a supported surface (its prior 'defect pending removal' row is removed from Known Defects), per the non-goal ADR 2026-08-23-non-goal-vet-specialty-filter.md.
integration_points: Vet.holdsSpecialty(String): whole-name case-insensitive membership test over the vet's specialties — the shared matching core, a domain query on the aggregate (keeps the rule in the model, not the controller)

VetController /vets.html: add @RequestParam(required=false) String specialty; normalize (strip; blank/whitespace -> no filter, mirroring OwnerController lines 98-104); read findAll() full list, filter by holdsSpecialty when a filter is present, paginate the filtered list in-memory via PageImpl(sublist, PageRequest.of(page-1,5), filteredSize); add normalized specialty (null when absent) to the model
VetController /vets JSON: add the same specialty param; filter the full list; addAll into a new Vets wrapper (never mutate the cached list)

vetList.html: paging links must carry the specialty — change @{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'} style links to Thymeleaf param form @{/vets.html(page=${i}, specialty=${specialty})} so a null specialty is omitted and unfiltered URLs stay clean
VetRepository.findAll(Pageable) becomes unused once HTML pages in-memory; remove it (this is why VetRepository is a file target)

patterns.description: precedent for optional filter param normalization (blank -> broadest) and the pagination model attributes (currentPage/totalPages/totalItems); reuse the normalization, but note the deliberate divergence: owner filters+pages at the DB, vet filters+pages in-code (see ADR)
Web controller row admits no business rule; put holdsSpecialty on Vet (Aggregate) so the controller stays orchestration-only — narrows, not widens, the recorded controller-rule gap

risks.risk: @WebMvcTest mocks VetRepository, so matching semantics are only meaningful if they execute in code the test drives; a repository derived query would make theSpecialtyFilterShouldMatchCaseInsensitively and theSpecialtyFilterShouldNotMatchOnAPrefix tautological
risks.mitigation: matching lives on Vet.holdsSpecialty and in the controller; stub findAll() to return real Vet+Specialty objects and assert real behavior. Also add VetTests unit tests for holdsSpecialty (case-insensitive match, whole-name-not-prefix, no-specialty vet) to seat the rule at the base of the pyramid

risks.risk: pagination-carry and multi-page acceptance criteria need more than one page of matches
risks.mitigation: stub findAll() with >5 vets holding the same specialty; assert the filtered result pages and that paging links carry specialty (model attribute present, template renders it)

risks.risk: in-place mutation of the cached 'vets' list would corrupt the shared cache (no eviction configured, Open Question 5)
risks.mitigation: filter by streaming into a new list; JSON path keeps the existing addAll-into-new-Vets shape

risks.risk: switching HTML from findAll(Pageable) to in-memory paging could change observable unfiltered behavior
risks.mitigation: same page size (5) and same underlying findAll() order preserve content/totalPages/totalItems; theUnfilteredVetPageShouldBehaveAsBefore guards it

notes: No foundational signals tripped; no conflict with the non-goal ADR (which explicitly admits this and reinstates the JSON surface). Testing note for the implementer: VetControllerTests uses @MockitoBean per the tolerated-legacy-mock allowance in testing-principles.md (Mocking Policy); extending that file with framework stubs is acceptable here, but new Vet unit tests use real value objects. Naming: holdsSpecialty follows ubiquitous-language.md ('the specialties they hold'). Ordering across filtered pages relies on findAll()'s default DB order, which is stable enough for this directory; not a blocker. No design-doc-autofix records present, so the autofix audit was a silent skip.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: No injection: the specialty filter runs in-memory over the @Cacheable('vets') findAll() list via Vet.holdsSpecialty (equalsIgnoreCase); no JPQL/SQL/query is constructed from user input on either surface

No reflected XSS: the normalized specialty is echoed only into the 'specialty' model attribute, consumed exclusively by Thymeleaf URL link expressions @{/vets.html(page=..,specialty=${specialty})} which URL-encode query-parameter values; it is never rendered into HTML text/attribute content

Cache/data integrity preserved: findMatchingVets copies findAll() into a new ArrayList and streams matches into a fresh list, and the JSON path addAll's into a new Vets wrapper; the shared cached collection is never mutated
Input normalization is safe: null/blank/whitespace collapse to no filter, no unsafe parsing or reflection on the value
Supply chain unchanged: no build.gradle or dependency changes in the change set, so no new CVE surface

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: findMatchingVets uses an explicit for-each accumulation loop where the checklist prefers a stream pipeline for transformations. The loop is correct but harder to read at a glance than a filter+collect chain.
findings.fix: Replace the loop body with: return allVets.stream().filter(v -> v.holdsSpecialty(specialty)).toList();

findings.description: Page size is a bare literal 5 with no named constant. The value is locally clear but a named constant (PAGE_SIZE) documents intent and makes future changes to a single place, consistent with how OwnerController handles the same literal.
findings.fix: Extract private static final int PAGE_SIZE = 5; and reference it throughout paginate().

findings.description: @GetMapping({ "/vets" }) wraps a single value in an unnecessary array literal. Spring accepts a plain string for single mappings.

Reviewer reached planned checkpoint (after first 3 production files) with VetTests.java and VetControllerTests.java not yet reviewed. Findings above cover Vet.java, VetController.java, VetRepository.java, and vetList.html only.

approved_aspects: holdsSpecialty is correctly placed on the Vet aggregate, keeping matching logic out of the controller — consistent with the Web-controller pattern in architecture-principles.md
Javadoc on holdsSpecialty precisely states whole-name case-insensitive semantics and distinguishes from prefix match
normalizeSpecialty null and blank handling mirrors OwnerController precedent as called out in the ADR
findMatchingVets never mutates the cached collection — copies into new ArrayList before any filtering

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Two PRD 'Done when' bullets for REQ-VET-003 specify 'either surface' but only the HTML surface is tested. Missing: (1) given a specialty matching no veterinarian, the JSON endpoint returns an empty vetList with HTTP 200; (2) given a blank or whitespace-only specialty, the JSON endpoint behaves as though no filter was given. The existing theSpecialtyFilterShouldYieldAnEmptyListWhenNoVetMatches and theBlankSpecialtyShouldBehaveAsNoFilter tests cover HTML only. A future regression in the JSON surface normalisation or filtering path would go undetected.

thePaginationLinksShouldCarryTheSpecialty contains a for-loop in the test body. The testing brief (§ Four-Phase Test Structure / § Agent Decision Checklist item 4) requires tests to be straight-line code with no loops. Replace the loop with a call to a factory helper or a stream-based collector at class level, or expand inline to the six literal factory calls.
findings.fix: Extract the surgeon-list construction to a private helper method (e.g., sixSurgeons()) and call it in the test body, removing the loop.

findings.description: The three new holdsSpecialty tests do not follow the BDD naming school the brief mandates for tests written from 2026-07-31 onward (§ Test Naming: the{Subject}Should{Outcome}). Current names: holdsSpecialtyMatchesTheWholeNameCaseInsensitively, holdsSpecialtyDoesNotMatchAPrefix, holdsSpecialtyIsFalseWhenTheVetHoldsNoSpecialty. Suggested renames: theVetShouldMatchASpecialtyByItsWholeNameCaseInsensitively, theVetShouldNotMatchASpecialtyOnAPrefix, theVetWithNoSpecialtyShouldNotMatchAnySpecialtyQuery.
findings.fix: Rename the three test methods to the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} form.

findings.description: New tests construct Vet with new Vet() directly. The brief (§ Test Data Construction / Factory Methods, effective 2026-07-31) requires all new tests to wrap construction in a factory method. A vetWithNoSpecialties() and a vetWithSpecialty(String) factory (complementing the private specialty() helper already present) would satisfy the rule and reduce duplication across the three new test methods.
findings.fix: Add private Vet vetWithNoSpecialties() and private Vet vetWithSpecialty(String name) factory methods; replace the inline new Vet() calls.

approved_aspects: Unit tests for holdsSpecialty correctly seat the matching rule at the base of the pyramid using real Vet and Specialty value objects — no mocks
@MockitoBean on VetRepository stays within the tolerated-legacy-mock allowance confirmed in the design-block and testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy
All new controller test names follow the{Subject}Should{Outcome} BDD school
Factory helpers james(), helen(), and vetWithSpecialty(int, String) wrap controller test construction correctly
AssertJ used throughout unit tests; Hamcrest matchers used only inside MockMvc result-matcher chains where the API requires them — both correct
Pyramid shape respected: holdsSpecialty logic is verified without framework boot in VetTests, and VetControllerTests wires it through without re-testing the matching semantics
theUnfilteredVetPageShouldBehaveAsBefore guards the regression risk noted in the design-block
All tests pass (./gradlew test exits 0)

author: change-grader
summary: filter vet directory by specialty on both surfaces

blast_radius.note: Reach is confined to the vet package plus its list template and tests; no sensitive paths, 6 of 12 files are docs, and the one real structural shift (dropping repository findAll(Pageable) for in-memory paging) stays inside that module.

semantic_surprise.note: Read the hunks: holdsSpecialty is null-safe whole-name case-insensitive as documented, normalizeSpecialty maps blank to no-filter, and paginate guards out-of-range pages (start>=size yields empty) with correct 1-to-0-based offset; null-specialty paths preserve prior all-vets behavior on both endpoints.

test_adequacy.note: Tests assert real outcomes on both surfaces (model hasSize/totalItems, JSON vetList sizes, content contains specialty=surgery on pagination links) and cover case-insensitivity, prefix non-match, empty result, blank-as-no-filter, and unfiltered baseline; Vet unit tests exercise the matcher directly.

reviewer_hedging.note: Full four-reviewer roster approved unanimously in R2 with no caveats; R1 findings (including the test-reviewer single-surface blocker and a code-quality truncation checkpoint) were all resolved before the clean re-approval.

scope_deviation.note: design_revisions=0, consultations=0, build_retries=0; the in-controller pagination re-architecture is the enabling means for filter-before-paginate, documented in an ADR, and the change delivers exactly the both-surfaces filter the requirement states.

rationale: All five facets clear on a diff read, not just the row. The one thing worth a glance is the deliberate move of pagination from a repository query to in-memory paging over the cached vet list (see the in-controller ADR); it is sound for this small cached set and the edge cases are guarded. Confirm and merge.
